remove: The three furrow strips as drawn: at actual size they read as more flattened agave leaves and a second hatch texture at lower left, not as a contour-ploughed Iowa field. Cut them, or redraw them so they cannot be mistaken for foliage. As they stand they are an extra device that fails its own job.
top_problem: This is ref-02 panel 3 re-set rather than a new idea: the same green ground, the same gold line agave, the same tracked CANTINA and the same gold tracked heads. The one element meant to make it ownable, the Iowa field fused into the agave, does not read at letter or phone size. The substitution test fails: this page could belong to any agave bar on the continent. The boldest missing idea is an Iowa landform the eye reads instantly: unmistakable contour-strip rows running to a horizon with the agave rising from them, or the furrows taking over as the page's structure and grid.
fixes: Make the Iowa half legible at thumbnail: give the furrows a horizon line, contour-strip curvature and an alternating hatch direction (strip cropping), so they read as field in under a second and not as leaves; otherwise the concept stays at about 64.

Give the dead top-right field a job: raise and extend the agave cone and spines into it (keeping 6 mm clearance), or shift the columns so that area becomes framed quiet space. Then even out the 71 px column-end mismatch by moving Cider to col 1's height, or by balancing the sections.

Upgrade the engraving craft: replace the vertical parallel-line fill in the cone and back leaves with contour-following hatch that swells and tapers (vary spacing, not stroke weight), so it reads as burin work rather than vector stripes beside ref-02's painterly and line agaves.

Tighten col 1 descriptions to at most 2 lines (widen col 1 by about 20 px, or set descriptions at 12 px), put both columns' item rows on one shared baseline increment, and match the top margin to the 64 px left margin.

Raise the H3 sub-labels from 9.5 to at least 10.5 CSS px (8 pt) for dim-bar legibility, drop the redundant 'By the Glass' (every wine is by the glass), and confirm the art extends at least 3 mm past trim in the print export.

lens: Items and prices against build/draft_doc.json; ingredient names and how complete the descriptions are (meta.public_components); section flow for a Mexican cantina and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The prices are all correct and the cocktails are fully described, but every item outside cocktails is described only as its category. 'Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour' and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' just repeat the item name. 'Dry red wine' gives no region, the beers give no ABV, and the spirits give no brand or age. None of these gaps is flagged as missing_ingredients. The design also puts Draft Beer below Wine and Spirits in a Mexican cantina, where beer is a main category, and Cider is a whole section for one item that ends the page. So only 4 of 15 items reach the criterion-8 standard. Checks: all 15 items and prices match the draft exactly (15/15/14/16, 12/16/18, 12/11/13, 7/8/7, 8), and nothing was invented or dropped. The Manhattan's Aromatic Bitters are correctly hidden (public_components false). The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel) are cited to phg.recipe_versions, not the draft, so the Accuracy reviewer should confirm them. The page has no taglines or prop captions. Every price is inline on its name's line, with 6-8% eye travel.
fixes: Flag missing_ingredients in doc.json for the region of all 3 wines, the ABV (and brewery, if known) of all 3 beers, the brand or age of the 2 tequilas and the Cognac, and the Dry Cider's producer and ABV. Until the Coordinator supplies that data, replace 'Blanco tequila pour' and 'VSOP Cognac pour' with neutral wording that doesn't just repeat the name, such as 'Unaged agave spirit, served neat' only if that is backed by data; otherwise keep the flag visible to the Coordinator.

Reorder the second column for a cantina as Draft Beer (the lagers first), then Wine, then Cider, or merge the single Dry Cider into the beer group as 'Beer & Cider', so the page doesn't end on a one-item section and beer isn't treated as secondary.
Merge the Margarita's orphaned third line 'Bright and citrus-forward' into the ingredient sentence (for example '... lime wheel. Bright and citrus-forward.') so it doesn't read as a separate tagline.

Give prices more visual weight than descriptions (they are currently the same muted #C9C2AF at 400 weight), for example the name's ivory at 500 with tabular figures, so price scanning stays tied to the name without competing with it.
Give the non-cocktail descriptions the same guest voice as the cocktail lines, with no taxonomy words like 'pour' or 'draft IPA', so the menu reads as one voice on the letter page and on the phone.

lens: Ingredient, garnish and label tracing against build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions; how descriptions sit with prices in preview-letter.png; the price-to-item gate
top_problem: Every printed fact traces, but half the menu has non-descriptions. 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour' and 'VSOP Cognac pour' only repeat the item name, and 'Dry red wine' / 'Dry white wine' are category labels with no grape detail, no region and no ABV. On top of that, the page reads as a generic hotel bar (Manhattan, Czech Pilsner, Malbec, Cognac) with an agave drawing on it. Apart from 'Añejo', nothing in the copy says Mexican cantina.

Spirits, wine, beer and cider descriptions and all 15 printed prices match phg.menu_items.menu_description / menu_price for project ddc4bb5b-70e6-4581-8aae-1b4042cd75ef; accents on Añejo and Brut Rosé match the source
Glassware (Rocks / Coupe) and method are in recipe_versions but not printed, so nothing is invented there
No tagline or prop caption on the page, so no item fact sits in brand copy
problems: Criterion 12: three spirit lines only restate the item name plus 'pour' (menu_items 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'). Because they come from the draft they are not invented, but they fail the 'never repeats the name' test and should have been flagged missing_ingredients (agave origin, age, house or brand), not printed as if they were descriptions.

Criterion 12: the Margarita is the only item with both a component list and a sentence ('Bright and citrus-forward'), so the menu speaks in two voices. Every other cocktail is a bare dot list, and the wine and beer lines are two-word category tags.

Criterion 11 (minor): source capitalisation was changed to sentence case ('Rye whiskey' vs Rye Whiskey, 'Brown butter-washed bourbon' vs Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon). The change is consistent and in guest register, but it is not the exact source spelling. The component order 'Tequila blanco' (draft) against the item name 'Blanco Tequila' on the same page also reads as an inconsistency to guests.
Criterion 8/11 gap not flagged: wine prints no grape detail or region, and beer prints no ABV, but the proposal raises no missing_ingredients request.

Unverified within the 6-call budget: menu_items also holds 'Junmai Ginjo' at 12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), and it is absent from the page. If it is in the draft doc, this is a missing item and content_integrity flips to fail. The Coordinator must confirm this against build/draft_doc.json.

Criterion 13: the venue is a Mexican cantina and cocktail bar in Iowa City, yet the section order puts Classics (Margarita, Manhattan) first, the agave list has only 2 pours, and the only Spanish anywhere is 'Añejo' and the wordmark. The draft limits the item list, but the kickers and sub-labels (Classics, House Originals, Agave, By the Glass) are editable venue wording and were left generic English.
Criterion 14: line breaks split ingredient phrases ('orange / liqueur', 'demerara / syrup' twice, 'cocktail / cherry' leaving 'cherry' as a one-word widow in the Manhattan).
Criterion 14: Brut Rosé 13 sits under the 'Sparkling' sub-label with no pour label. 'By the glass' only covers the still wines above, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle price.

Criterion 14 / gate: inline prices sit 0.9 em after each name on the name line (eye travel 6-8% of the column), and no description touches a price. The association gate passes. The price and the description share the same muted #C9C2AF, so the price gets no emphasis beyond its position.
fixes: Replace the three name-echo spirit descriptions with a missing_ingredients request for age, agave or region, and brand, and until the rows arrive, print no description rather than a restatement of the name.
Give every cocktail the same structure (component list plus at most one sourced sentence, or component list only) so the Margarita tail no longer reads as a different voice.
Bind ingredient phrases with non-breaking spaces (orange liqueur, demerara syrup, cocktail cherry, lime wheel) so no ingredient splits across lines and no one-word widow remains.
Add a 'Glass' label (or carry 'By the glass' over the Sparkling group) so the Brut Rosé 13 price is unambiguous, and ask for wine grape/region and beer ABV rows before printing.
Confirm whether Junmai Ginjo (menu_items, 12) is in the draft doc; if it is, it must appear or its removal must be sourced.
